articles.title: "Riding the rollercoaster": Drake Maye reveals biggest regret from Eagles joint practice
articles.standfirst: The Patriots star praised Jalen Hurts and acknowledged the area New England needs to fix
articles.summary: The Patriots star praised Jalen Hurts and acknowledged the area New England needs to fix
articles.body:
The encouraging part for Drake Maye is that joint practices with the Philadelphia Eagles no longer feel like a measuring stick the New England Patriots are failing. The frustrating part is that he knows they could have been better.

After a strong opening session Wednesday, Maye endured a more uneven Thursday that included two interceptions and several red-zone snaps he wanted back.

One of those picks came on a throw intended for A.J. Brown , making the missed opportunity stand out even more as the two continue building chemistry.

“I think we had a lot of great work,” Maye said after practice. “I think the biggest thing is that is a good football team over there, and I think just not riding the rollercoaster.”

That became his biggest takeaway from the two days in that New England showed it could compete with Philadelphia, but not yet with the consistency Maye wants.

“I feel like we had some good periods that we were attacking them and had some good plays,” he said. “Then we had some periods where we got to continue the competitive stamina.”

Red-zone mistakes left Maye wanting more

Thursday was hardly a disaster. Maye still threw touchdowns to Brown , Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs , and the Patriots held their own against one of the league’s deeper defenses.

Still, the quarterback was clearly bothered by the chances that disappeared close to the goal line.

“I know it's tough down there in the red zone, a lot of bodies in a short amount of space, but I feel like we could have done more in the red zone,” Maye said. “It's one of our focuses this year to be better in the red zone, so we got some work to do.”

The performance came one day after he opened Wednesday by completing his first 13 passes, illustrating how quickly momentum can shift during competitive practice periods.

It also gave Maye another reason to appreciate how far the Patriots have come since the Eagles visited Foxborough during his rookie year.

“I was watching some of those plays earlier in the week. I was just laughing,” Maye said. “Little things like that, that we were laughing about, just how far we have come.”

Hurts gives Maye another standard to chase

After practice, Maye sought out Jalen Hurts before leaving the field.

The Patriots quarterback has followed Hurts’ career for years and said he respects both his success and the work ethic behind it.

“I'm a big fan of his game. Rooting for him,” Maye said. “He's a Super Bowl champ. That speaks for itself.”

One of Maye’s close friends, Sam Howell , previously shared a quarterback room with Hurts , giving Maye another perspective on how the Philadelphia star prepares.

“I got to know some stories about Jalen and how he works,” Maye said. “I respect him a lot for that. I'm pulling for him.”

That focus on preparation fits where Maye is entering Year 3. The Patriots are clearly better than they were two years ago. Now the standard has shifted.

Being competitive is no longer enough. The mistakes Maye regrets are becoming the details that could decide how far New England goes.

articles.title: No love lost between Tom Brady and Patriots: Josh McDaniels and Robert Spillane fire back at franchise legend
articles.standfirst: Brady's comments before last season's Super Bowl clearly didn't sit right with the New England organization.
articles.summary: Brady's comments before last season's Super Bowl clearly didn't sit right with the New England organization.
articles.body:
Since the turn of the 21st century, there wasn't a better pairing in all of football than Tom Brady and Bill Belichick on the New England Patriots . It was a fairytale story from the get-go.

Brady was a sixth round pick, biding his time until his golden moment came. Once it did, Brady and the Patriots couldn't stop winning . After six Super Bowls together , Brady eventually moved on, but he remained close to the organization. Then came last season's Super Bowl .

The Patriots were aiming to win the seventh in their history, and their first without Brady. Despite their cherished time together, Brady gave a surprising statement when talking about Super Bowl LX between the Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks : " I don't have a dog in the fight ".

Tom Brady sitting on the fence during Seahawks-Patriots Super Bowl remains in New England's mind

This week, Brady's comments resurfaced among the Pats organization, thanks to interviews on WEEI with Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels and linebacker Robert Spillane .

McDaniels was asked if he thinks Brady helped the Seahawks against the Patriots in the Super Bowl. McDaniels gave a tongue-in-cheek reply: " I have no idea. I wouldn't have a dog in that fight ".

Spillane was much more fired up when talking about Brady's comment: " It irritated me, and it made me feel sad for him, spending 20 years here, obviously, went on to do amazing, great things, not only on the football field but in the community, and to say that he had no care in the world, it irritated me ".

Clearly, Brady sitting on the fence rubbed many Patriots members and fans the wrong way.

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski gives his Massachusetts mansion a jaw-dropping upgrade
articles.standfirst: The new design now includes dedicated entertainment areas, including a s'mores station
articles.summary: The new design now includes dedicated entertainment areas, including a s'mores station
articles.body:
Rob Gronkowski built a Hall of Fame-caliber NFL career on big plays, big celebrations, and an even bigger personality. Now, the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star is bringing that same energy to his home life.

Gronkowski and longtime partner Camille Kostek recently unveiled a major renovation project at their custom Massachusetts mansion, transforming their backyard into what may be one of the ultimate entertaining spaces in New England.

The upgraded outdoor area features a fully equipped kitchen, expansive gathering spaces, and amenities designed specifically for hosting the couple's large circle of family and friends. For Gronkowski and Kostek, the project wasn't just about luxury.

It was about creating a space that matched the way they actually live. "We just redid the interior of our house, and I felt like the backyard was the next project," Kostek said. "This is the beginning of the transformation of our backyard, and now I'm more excited to host."

From makeshift gatherings to a backyard built for entertaining

Before the renovation, the couple relied on a much simpler setup whenever they hosted guests. According to Kostek , outdoor gatherings often involved ice coolers, a standalone grill, and improvised serving areas scattered around the yard. "We had a lot of ice coolers outside and a standing grill, but we never had a place for everything," she explained.

We had a lot of ice coolers outside and a standing grill, but we never had a place for everything," she explained. The limitations became especially noticeable whenever Gronkowski's massive extended family came to visit. The former Patriots tight end has nine nieces and nephews, and summer gatherings regularly turn into large family events.

The new design now includes dedicated entertainment areas, including a s'mores station located near the property's bonfire space. "Rob has about nine nieces and nephews, and when they all come over in the summer, now we have a s'mores station instead of setting everything up on chairs and on the ground," Kostek said . For a player who spent years bringing crowds to their feet at Gillette Stadium, creating a better space for family gatherings became a natural next step.

Gronk wanted something simple and durable

Anyone who followed Gronkowski's career knows he appreciates efficiency almost as much as touchdowns. The four-time Super Bowl champion admitted that ease of installation played a major role in the couple's decision to partner with RTA Outdoor Living for the project.

"I'm that guy when it becomes difficult, I'm like, 'All right, I'm good with this, I want something that's easy to set up and easy to build,'" Gronkowski said. The former NFL star was impressed by how quickly the project came together.

Having spent most of his NFL career in New England, Gronkowski knows better than anyone how unpredictable the region's weather can be. "Being up here in New England, you've got all types of weather. You've got snow, rain and sleet. It can withstand it all," he said. "It's very sturdy, very durable, and you don't have to worry about replacing products every single year."

A backyard designed around family

The centerpiece of the makeover is a custom outdoor kitchen tailored to the couple's entertaining style. The setup includes two 12-foot islands that separate cooking and gathering areas, creating a natural flow for parties and family events. There is also a dedicated pizza oven station, built-in refrigeration, storage space, an ice chest, and integrated trash compartments.

For Kostek , the design process was almost as enjoyable as the finished product. She also selected design elements intended to connect the outdoor space with the home's recently renovated interior, choosing a white plank-style finish complemented by Thunder White granite and stainless steel features.

The result is a backyard that feels like a seamless extension of the home rather than a separate entertainment area. The renovated backyard sits within one of Gronkowski's most impressive real estate holdings.

The former Patriots star owns a custom-built mansion in F oxboro, Massachusetts , located near the community where he became one of the most beloved athletes in franchise history. The property spans nearly 4,500 square feet and includes five bedrooms, three bathrooms, a swimming pool, and a spa.

articles.title: “We don’t have a very deep team”: Mike Vrabel’s words that made waves with the Patriots
articles.standfirst: The NFL preseason usually leaves more questions than answers, and not even a victory can disguise the weaknesses.
articles.summary: The NFL preseason usually leaves more questions than answers, and not even a victory can disguise the weaknesses.
articles.body:
After the game where the Eagles triumphed over Philadelphia, the coach spoke about his team's depth and then clarified that his words were not a message to the front office. Mike Vrabel left a remark that quickly drew attention after the New England Patriots ’ 24-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles . The coach did not mince words when asked about his decisions during the preseason.

After the Patriots ' victory over the Eagles , Mike justified the absence of several starters with a specific phrase: “I don’t think we have a very deep team” . The statement could leave another question on the table: Was it a direct jab at management demanding signings?

“We are the front office”

This Monday, the Patriots head coach appeared on The Greg Hill Show and expanded on his remarks. There, he was asked directly whether his comment about the roster's depth had been a message to the New England front office.

“We are the front office," Vrabel answered. "We are all making the decisions. We’re all included in this. It was about the young guys we have to develop. You can see that the players we kept out of the game, those are the guys. And we have to be able to find some guys behind them to be backups, to be the first guy in. To be the third outside linebacker. Be the third inside linebacker. Be the sixth offensive lineman. These things that are so critical. Be the third safety

The coach made it clear that he was talking about the development process of young players. The football players who were left out of the game were precisely some of the starters the Patriots need to protect, while the challenge is to prepare those behind them to take on an important role if needed.

Vrabe l admitted to having spoken that same morning with Eliot Wolf, the team's director of personnel, to align their strategy. He assured that there is no internal conflict. The coaching staff knows perfectly well what is on the roster, and although the priority remains to maximize young talent in practices, the market door is not closed.

“So those are the things that we are trying to develop, and I guess that’s what I was referencing. I can walk back, and I’ve already talked to (executive vice president of player personnel) Eliot (Wolf) this morning, and these aren’t issues. I’m not in a subtle context – that wasn’t that. They asked why we didn’t play the guys, and we have to have everybody we have available and then continue to develop and see some guys that went out and played like they did on Saturday night to continue to build that depth.

What having depth means for Vrabel

Vrabel's explanation makes that initial statement easier to understand. The coach is thinking about the players who must come in when a starter is out and believes that those footballers need to be prepared to take on an important role.

"The reason is simple: during an NFL season, starters cannot play in every game and every snap. Injuries and game situations make it necessary to use the backups, so Vrabel wants those players to be ready to come in without the team’s functioning changing too much.

The Patriots coach still expects answers

Just days before the final roster cutdown, New England is caught in a race against the clock: finding those answers on its own training camp field or scrambling to look for them on the league’s cut list. The coach did not rule out the possibility that New England could look for players outside the current roster. The Patriots could be evaluating signings, waivers, or trades as the cut that will define the roster draws near.

But the priority is also within the team itself. The preseason is precisely for finding out which young players can take that step and become real alternatives for the season. Something that the coach and the front office currently have as their main objective.

articles.title: The investigation into the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel scandal takes a new turn
articles.standfirst: A potential NFL-media partnership is raising fresh questions about the unresolved review
articles.summary: A potential NFL-media partnership is raising fresh questions about the unresolved review
articles.body:
The controversy surrounding former NFL insider Dianna Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has largely disappeared from the daily football conversation, but one important question remains unanswered: what exactly will The Athletic ultimately conclude about Russini’s reporting?

That question has gained renewed attention because The Athletic is now reportedly discussing a deeper commercial relationship with the NFL, potentially creating an awkward overlap between the league and an outlet that has spent months examining whether one of its former reporters had a conflict of interest involving an NFL head coach.

The original controversy erupted in April after photographs emerged showing Russini and Vrabel together at a resort in Arizona.

Images appeared to show the pair holding hands, embracing and spending time together around a pool and hot tub. Both Russini and Vrabel initially disputed the suggestion that the photographs demonstrated a romantic relationship.

Russini said the images failed to show the larger group she said was present, while Vrabel described the interaction as “completely innocent.”

The Athletic initially defended Russini , with executive editor Steven Ginsberg saying the photographs were “misleading and lack essential context.”

The situation changed when The Athletic began a formal review of Russini’s conduct and reporting. She was sidelined while the investigation continued before ultimately resigning from the organization on April 14.

At the time, she maintained that she stood behind her journalism and rejected the narrative that had developed around the photographs.

Vrabel , meanwhile, remained with the Patriots . He acknowledged that the controversy had resulted in difficult conversations with his family and members of the organization, and he subsequently missed the third day of the NFL Draft while beginning counseling.

The NFL itself did not launch an investigation into Vrabel's conduct. An NFL spokesman confirmed in April that the league was not examining the Patriots coach over the incident.

The NFL partnership is creating an uncomfortable timing problem

The latest development involves The Athletic rather than Vrabel or Russini directly.

Front Office Sports reported on August 21 that NFL Media and The Athletic have discussed expanding their existing relationship, with the possibility of Athletic articles appearing on NFL.com or through the NFL+ app.

Neither side publicly commented on the discussions, and it remains unclear how advanced negotiations are.

That timing has inevitably prompted questions about the unresolved Russini investigation. If The Athletic is scrutinizing whether a former reporter compromised journalistic standards through an alleged relationship with an NFL coach, critics can reasonably ask how an increasingly close relationship with the league would affect perceptions of that review.

OutKick's Armando Salguero highlighted precisely that concern, writing: “The Athletic is presumably in the throes of this conflict of interest investigation of a former reporter with an NFL coach while at the same time engaging in talks to enter into a conflict of interest situation with the NFL. Got it,”

The concern is not necessarily that a partnership would alter the investigation. There is currently no public evidence demonstrating that it would. Instead, the issue is one of perception and editorial independence.

The Athletic has previously said its investigation was taking time because there was substantial material to examine.

In June, Ginsberg reportedly told staff that the process would take “a few more weeks,” while promising that the organization would provide an update once it reached the end of its review.

More than two months later, the findings have still not been publicly released.

The controversy has also continued to affect Russini professionally. In June, she described the episode as having a “significant impact” on her personal and professional life and referred to herself as a “former journalist” in communications with a New York Times reporter.

For now, the investigation remains unresolved, while Vrabel has returned to the normal demands of coaching the Patriots.

The NFL season has shifted attention back toward football, but the eventual outcome of The Athletic's review could still have consequences for its credibility, Russini's legacy and the outlet's relationship with the league.

The unanswered question is therefore no longer simply what happened between Russini and Vrabel . It is also whether The Athletic can complete and communicate its findings in a way that leaves no doubt about the independence of its process.

articles.summary: The Patriots prepare for the 2026-2027 season in a home matchup with Cleveland
articles.body:
The NFL preseason is entering its final stretch, and one of the most attractive matchups on the schedule pits the Cleveland Browns against the New England Patriots .

The NFL preseason is a period when the spotlight is not on established stars but on the backups, the rookies fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster and the coaching staffs looking for answers before the regular season kicks off.

Preseason does not award standings points or decide playoff berths, but it does shape rosters. Both Cleveland and New England arrive at this late-August window using the matchup as a laboratory : broad rotations, short series for the starters—when they play at all—and extended minutes for those fighting for a contract.

For the Browns, playing at home adds the incentive of showing progress to their fans before the official kickoff. For the Patriots, it is just another road stop in a month of pure evaluation.

What time is the Browns vs Patriots game?

The matchup between New England and Cleveland is scheduled for this Thursday, August 27, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. EST Eastern Time; in the rest of the country, the game will start at the following times:

The preseason game will be played at FirstEnergy Stadium, in the city of Cleveland , United States, a venue with a capacity of 67,895 spectators on the shores of Lake Erie.

Home-field advantage carries relative weight in the preseason, but the setting and atmosphere are still those of an NFL stadium .

How will you be able to watch the Browns vs Patriots game live?

For NFL fans around the world who follow every game from the preseason onward, the broadcast is handled by DAZN and NFL Game Pass.

Particularly, in the United States and specifically locally in Boston and Cleveland, it will be available on the following channels and streaming services :

TV channel : WCVB Channel 5 and WEWS-TV Channel 5

Streaming Services : Prime Video and NFL+

How is the betting market for the preseason game between the Browns and Patriots?

Here it is best to be honest: preseason matchups are, by definition, the hardest to predict on the entire schedule . Sportsbook lines for these games usually open late and move sharply as soon as word gets out about which starters will rest and how much the second- and third-string units will play.

A favorite on paper can become a loser if it decides to rest its key pieces while the rival gives minutes to players hungry for a roster spot.

Given that the official lines for this Browns vs Patriots game are not yet available on the market, these recommendations take a strategic approach. Adjust the exact figures when the board opens:

Under on total points — the strongest market in preseason; offenses tend to start slowly and coaching staffs limit their playbooks. Wait for the line and take the Under if it opens at a high number.

Short point spread — avoid paying a premium for a favorite. If Cleveland, at home, opens as a slight favorite, the value is on underdog New England getting points, given the unpredictability of the second half.

Second half — team with better depth — betting on the performance of the reserve units in the final stretch usually offers more value than the overall result, since that’s where the game is truly decided.

The key, as always in the preseason, is discipline: bet small, bet late, and let lineup information do half the work for you.
